column1: # Hand-decided renames: old <TAB> new [<TAB> path:line]. With a path:line, the row renames only
# the declaration there (a name with different meanings in different places); without one it
# renames every declaration of the name. new == old keeps the name.
# Assembler (asm = the assembler) and assembly code.
# Floating point (fp), and fp as a FILE* or port (all the fp variables are files).
# The operand-shape tags of opcode-types.tsv for floating-point instructions: FLOATING_POINT once,
# then the manual's fields (fd destination, fs source, ft target, fr addend).
# Integers (int = integer) and interrupts (INT in the console device and exception names).
# Coprocessor 0 (decision 1). Register accessors read like variables, so they are lower case;
# register numbers, bit masks and fields are upper-case constants.
# Exception codes (the Cause register's ExcCode field).
# Floating-point control registers: FCR the control registers, FIR implementation, FCSR control
# and status. Field constants drop the trailing "register".
# Registers a student names in assembly (decision 2): spelled out by meaning.
# hi and lo: the explain snapshot's HI/LO copies, and elsewhere the high and low end of a range.
# Instruction modifiers (MOD_<suffix letter>_<meaning>): the suffix letter is the mnemonic's.
# op: an opcode token, except the operator characters of the constant-expression parser.
# pseudo-op is the assembler's own term (teaching mode prints it); kept.
# The bit-string buffers of the explain layouts (b_ = the bits of a field) and their fields.
# Shift amount, identifiers, input, callbacks, comparisons.
# Kept: English words, or decided by decision 5 (the long-hand multiply).
# Kernel segments (k = kernel), and the byte and half-word views of a segment.
# Single-letter fields: renamed only at their declaration (the letter is a loop variable elsewhere).
# Kernel segments (k = kernel); the half-word (h) and byte (b) views of a segment; unsigned (u);
# The assembler's location counters (where the next datum or instruction goes), not the CPU's PC.
# Two spellings meant the same thing; the merged name needs one row (parse_expr parses a sum).
